evidence.quote: Small interfering RNA-mediated knockdown of Ctdnep1 increased tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase-positive multinucleated osteoclasts and the expression of osteoclast marker genes, including Acp5, Ctsk, and Nfatc1.
Ctdnep1 phosphatase is required for negative regulation of RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation in RAW264.7 cells.

experiment.endpoint: osteoclast differentiation / TRAP-positive multinucleated osteoclasts and marker gene expression
experiment.intervention: small interfering RNA-mediated knockdown of Ctdnep1

claim.summary: Small interfering RNA knockdown of Ctdnep1 increased osteoclast differentiation-related phenotypes in RANKL-induced RAW264.7 cells, including more TRAP-positive multinucleated osteoclasts and higher osteoclast marker expression.
uncertainties: The text links the observation to RANKL-induced RAW264.7 cells, but the species is not explicitly stated in the supplied passage.
Ctdnep1 is treated as a gene-level perturbation target here; the text also refers to the phosphatase protein, so molecular form is not fully disambiguated.
The title states negative regulation, but the extracted claim is limited to the observed knockdown effect and does not assert direct mechanism.
